explanation:
[EFFECT] The year feature acts like an on/off switch: in 2011 (yr = 0) it consistently pulls predicted demand **down**, with contributions clustered around –0.25 to –0.35 in log space; in 2012 (yr = 1) it consistently pushes demand **up**, with contributions clustered around +0.15 to +0.20. The shape is a clear step change — there is no gradual transition, just two distinct levels — and the peak effect (highest contribution) occurs in 2012. In practice this means the model predicts meaningfully more rentals in 2012 than in 2011, all else being equal.

[IMPORTANCE] Year is the **second most important** feature in the model (importance score 0.200), just ahead of temperature (0.197) and well behind only the hour of the day (0.833). It has a strong, consistent influence on predicted demand across the entire dataset.

[RECOMMENDATION] When planning capacity or staffing for a future period, account for a systematic growth trend: if ridership has been rising year over year, the model will forecast noticeably higher demand in later years, so bike availability and staffing levels should be scaled up accordingly rather than using prior-year figures as a direct baseline.
